Class Button

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.AbstractPanelElement<Button>
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.Button
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class Button extends AbstractPanelElement<Button>
An interactive button within a Panel. Renders a raised panel background with centered text. Supports hover detection, a click handler, and an optional disabled predicate.

This is MenuKit's core button abstraction. The default form renders centered text on a raised panel background. An icon-only variant is available via icon(int, int, int, Identifier, Consumer) and its supplier overload.

Left-click only by default. Right-clicks and middle-clicks fall through to vanilla's slot handling. Custom element implementations can handle any mouse button.

Construction — prefer spec(int, int, Component, Consumer) / .at(x,y)

The positional constructors take childX/childY as their leading arguments. The fluent path keeps the position out of the argument list and reads cleaner: use spec(int, int, Component, Consumer) to drop a button into a Row/Column layout (which computes its position), or construct without a position and call .at(x, y) + .size(w, h). The positional constructors remain for the cases where threading (x, y) through the constructor is the clearest spelling; they are not deprecated, just no longer the only path.

Rendering styles:

  • Normal: raised panel background, white text with shadow
  • Hovered: raised panel background + translucent highlight, white text
  • Pressed: inset panel background (sunken bevel) while a left-click is held — a tactile "the player is pushing this button" affordance. Cleared on release
  • Disabled: dark panel background, gray text

Extension points for consumer subclasses

Consumer code can customize Button rendering by subclassing and overriding the protected hooks: renderBackground(RenderContext, int, int) and renderContent(RenderContext, int, int). Those methods carry a stability contract — their signatures and semantic contracts are maintained across MenuKit versions. See their javadocs for the contract details.

The top-level render(RenderContext) is final — it orchestrates hover-state update, background paint, content paint, and tooltip dispatch in that order. The extension surface is the hooks, not the orchestration.

    • layoutWithin

      public void layoutWithin(int budget)
      Resolve to the panel-assigned budget: shrink the box to min(natural, budget) so the button never bleeds past the panel, THEN wrap the label across multiple lines when the narrowed box is too small for the label on one line. This is the documented contract (PanelElement#layoutWithin): a Button "shrinks its box to the budget and wraps its label across multiple lines, growing taller to fit."

      Wrap is engaged ONLY when the box's inner text area is narrower than the label's natural single-line width — at a roomy budget the wrap clears (wrapWidth = 0) so the button reports its authored single-line height again. A later wider pass therefore un-wraps it, fully REVERSIBLY (mirrors TextLabel.layoutWithin(int)).

      Parameters:
      budget - horizontal pixels available to this element, in panel content space. Always >= 1.

    • extraLayoutHeight

      public int extraLayoutHeight()
      Extra vertical pixels this button occupies BEYOND its authored box height because its label wrapped under layoutWithin(int) — i.e. getHeight() - authoredHeight when wrapped, else 0. The owning Panel reflows the elements below this button downward by exactly this amount, so a button that grows from one line to two pushes — never paints over — what's beneath it (mirrors TextLabel.extraLayoutHeight()).

    • renderBackground

      protected void renderBackground(RenderContext ctx, int sx, int sy)
      Paints the button's panel background — raised when enabled, dark when disabled, plus a translucent highlight overlay when hovered. Called before renderContent(RenderContext, int, int).

      Stable extension point for consumer Button subclasses. The signature (RenderContext ctx, int sx, int sy) and the semantic contract — sx/sy are the absolute screen-space top-left of the button, this hook runs before renderContent(RenderContext, int, int), this hook does not mutate Button state — are maintained across MenuKit versions. Consumer subclasses may rely on these properties.

      Override this hook to paint a custom background while keeping the default content rendering, or call super.renderBackground(...) and layer additional painting on top.

    • renderContent

The signature (RenderContext ctx, int sx, int sy) and the semantic contract — sx/sy are the absolute screen-space top-left of the button, this hook runs after renderBackground(RenderContext, int, int), this hook does not mutate Button state — are maintained across MenuKit versions. Consumer subclasses may rely on these properties.

      Override this hook to paint custom content (icon, multi-line text, composite visuals) while keeping the default panel-style background.

    • mouseReleased

      public boolean mouseReleased(double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      Clears the press-affordance state on left-button release. Fires regardless of cursor position (the dispatcher routes release events un-hit-tested per PanelElement.mouseReleased(double, double, int)), so a press-then-drag-off still releases the visual depression. Returns false — release isn't "consumed" in the usual sense; we just piggyback on the dispatch to reset cosmetic state.
      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X at release
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y at release
      button - mouse button (0=left, 1=right, 2=middle)
      Returns:
      true if consumed (rare for release events)

    • icon

      public static Button icon(int childX, int childY, int size, net.minecraft.resources.Identifier sprite, Consumer<Button> onClick)
      Creates a square Button that renders a centered sprite instead of a text label. Size is a single int (square only).

      The sprite is inset 2px from the button's edges so the panel-style border (RAISED bevel, INSET sunken edge) remains visible around the icon. When the button is disabled, the sprite is dimmed to ~40% alpha as an accessibility signal; hover/pressed states are communicated by the panel-style background shift.

      Accessibility: Icon-only buttons convey meaning through sprite alone, which can be less discoverable than text labels. Pairing Button.icon with a tooltip via AbstractPanelElement.tooltip(Component) or AbstractPanelElement.tooltip(Supplier) is strongly recommended for accessibility and discoverability. Users hovering over an icon button should learn its purpose from the tooltip.

      For a sprite that swaps based on consumer state, use the supplier overload.

      Parameters:
      childX - X position within panel content area
      childY - Y position within panel content area
      size - width and height in pixels (square)
      sprite - the sprite identifier to render
      onClick - fired on left-click when enabled

    • sprite

      public static Button sprite(int childX, int childY, int width, int height, net.minecraft.resources.Identifier sprite, net.minecraft.network.chat.Component label, Consumer<Button> onClick)
      Creates a Button whose entire background is a consumer-supplied sprite, replacing the default RAISED / INSET / DARK panel styles. The sprite is responsible for the whole button look — frame, fill, any decoration. Use this when the default panel-style chrome doesn't fit (themed buttons, embossed buttons, sprite-art buttons, etc.).

      Per-state rendering:

      • Normal: sprite drawn as-is.
      • Hovered: sprite + translucent white overlay (same hover affordance as the default Button).
      • Pressed: sprite rendered through a custom GLSL pipeline that inverts each pixel's HSL lightness while preserving hue and saturation. Blacks → whites, dark blues → light blues, light greys → dark greys. Reads as "this button is being pushed down" without relying on a separate pressed-state texture.
      • Disabled: sprite + dark translucent overlay (~50% black).

      Optional text label sits on top of the sprite, centered, using the same font/color rules as a default Button. Pass Component.empty() for a sprite-only button.

      Parameters:
      childX - X position within panel content area
      childY - Y position within panel content area
      width - button width in pixels
      height - button height in pixels
      sprite - the sprite identifier to use as the button background
      label - centered text label, or Component.empty() for sprite-only
      onClick - fired on left-click when enabled
